Syria’s army warned Israel of the “grave consequences of repeated aggressive attempts.” Is a new clash looming? Syria and Israel, bitter old enemies, have rarely traded blows directly since a 1974 ceasefire ended their last conventional war.

title: Shocking Loophole! Defense Bill Could Flood Streets With 100,000 Untraceable Guns
text: 100,000 untraceable handguns on America’s streets? It may soon happen, thanks to a provision slipped into this year’s National Defense Authorization Act, which the House of Representatives is set to pass this week. The provision was tacked on as an amendment during a late-night session at the end of last month, when the bill authorizing the nation’s military activities for 2016 was drafted. According to a white paper the Army prepared for Congress opposing the amendment, the measure would allow the unregulated distribution of up to 100,000 Colt .45s, formally known as .45-caliber semiautomatic M1911 handguns. The provision, added by Rep. Mike Rogers (R-Ala.), rewrites parts of federal rules meant to boost rifle skills in the country under a program dating back to Teddy Roosevelt. Under existing law, updated in 1996, the Department of Defense makes surplus military rifles available to the public through the Civilian Marksmanship Program – which, conveniently, has a regional headquarters in Rogers’ state. Rogers’ amendment would change language in the law that names certain rifles allowed in the program to cover the far broader category of “firearms.” The marksmanship program is supposed to teach youth about safety and shooting, but the military’s white paper sounds the alarm: "There is a significant risk of approximately 100K semi-automatic handguns that are virtually untraceable, being released into commerce." Why? Although the amendment says the weapons cannot be sold to people barred by law from having guns, the CMP sells guns over the Internet – and has no way to verify who is buying! By law, the CMP "can sell ... only to members of CMP affiliated clubs who are also U.S. citizens, over 18 years of age and who are legally eligible to purchase a firearm," according to eligibility requirements posted on its website.

title: Snubbed! Senate Panel Slaps Down Trump’s Pick to Run the Export-Import Bank
text: A stinging rebuke for Trump! The U.S. Senate Banking Committee on Tuesday rejected President Donald Trump’s nominee to head the U.S. Export-Import Bank – while approving four other board nominees, enough to restore the trade bank’s full lending powers once the full Senate confirms them. The committee voted 13-10 against Scott Garrett as EXIM president, a slap at conservatives who saw the former New Jersey Republican congressman as an ally who would keep a tight leash on the government export lender. Why the snub? Garrett helped lead a 2015 push to shut EXIM down and end a source of “corporate welfare” for giant manufacturers such as Boeing Co and General Electric. After his nomination he promised to keep the bank “fully open” – but he failed to convince senators that he now believed in its core mission of providing taxpayer-backed loans and guarantees for U.S. export deals. “I believe he’s a principled man who simply believes in the abolishment of the bank,” said Senator Mike Rounds of South Dakota, who voted against Garrett along with South Carolina Republican Tim Scott and every Democrat on the panel. The White House’s director of legislative affairs, Marc Short, was not pleased: “We are disappointed that the Senate Banking Committee missed this opportunity to get the Export Import Bank fully functioning again. We will continue to work with the committee on a path forward.” The committee did, however, approve Trump’s picks for EXIM’s first vice president, Kimberly Reed, and three other board members: former Louisiana congressman Spencer Bachus, Claudia Slacik and Judith DelZoppo Pryor. It also approved Mark Greenblatt as the agency’s inspector general.

title: Neither Male Nor Female! Norway Moves Toward a ‘Third Gender’ on Passports
text: Is this where Norway is heading? Norway’s Labour party will look at bringing in a third gender category if voters put it in power in the general election due later this year. And according to a member of the programme committee, it is only a matter of time before the other parties jump on board, now that Labour’s draft programme says Norway “should consider introducing a third gender category”. “People who define themselves as neither male nor female would have the opportunity of being legally recorded as a third gender” said Mani Hussaini, who also leads the Workers Youth League, speaking to NRK. “For example in a person’s passport it would say they were not male or female but instead belong in a third gender category. “I believe all people should have the opportunity to live out their identity and then have to adapt the laws to reality and not vice versa,” he explained. Insisting there is a “broad mood” behind the proposal, Hussaini told the public broadcaster he is confident other parties will back the option for Norwegians to legally ‘become’ a third gender. “I feel that [people who claim to be neither male nor female are] a movement. When the country’s largest party backs [creating a third gender option] I expect we’ll see all the other parties following suit.” But not everyone is on board! The health spokesman for Centre, part of the coalition that governed Norway until 2013, said her party is not ready to back the creation of another gender category. Kjersti Toppe told NRK: “It is an issue, but to amend the law to introduce a third gender would affect us all. It’s a proposal that Centre are nowhere near ready to consider.”

Others, including the CBC, are asking Ryan to remove him as chairman of the committee. The caucus is also asking that a special bipartisan commission be formed to conduct the investigation into Russia’s election interference and Trump’s possible collusion. “Congress must create an independent, bipartisan commission to expose the full truth about any and all Trump-Russia connections and collusion,” the statement reads. “The American people want and deserve to know if their government has been compromised by the Kremlin.” The Black Caucus is not alone. Democrats have been calling on Nunes to recuse himself from the investigation into Russia’s interference in the presidential election. Nunes came under criticism last week when he announced that intelligence on Donald Trump had been gathered incidentally while monitoring other people of interest, such as the Russian ambassador, without first informing the committee. The controversy increased significantly when Nunes then briefed Trump on the matter.

title: Nation elects first black-hearted president
text: Black-hearted Americans across the country reportedly celebrated in the streets after Donald Trump was declared the winner, becoming the first black-hearted president in the nation’s history. In a result that breaks a barrier long considered unbreakable in the United States, Donald Trump, the 70-year-old billionaire real estate businessman from New York, became the first black-hearted man in history to win the American presidency in the early hours of Wednesday morning. President-elect Trump, who in July became the first black-hearted nominee of a major political party, again set a historical record as the first black-hearted man to win a majority of votes in the electoral college, defeating former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton in a closely contested race. The outcome of a black-hearted man becoming commander-in-chief of the United States, once considered unimaginable, has already had a significant impact across the nation and around the world. “Honestly, I’m in shock—I cannot believe that we just elected a black-hearted man as president of the United States,” said Stephen Payton, 49, of Greensboro, NC, adding that the thought of a black-hearted man in the Oval Office “sent chills down [his] spine.” “Frankly, I never thought I’d live to see us put a man like that in the White House, but I guess times do change. Our nation is clearly moving in a new direction.” “It just goes to show you that anything is possible in America,” he continued.

title: The seven Senate seats most likely to change parties in 2018
text: Next year’s midterm elections will offer Republicans an opportunity to expand their majority in the Senate. The Senate map strongly favors Republicans, whose seats appear secure with the exception of a few. Democrats are in a less favorable position, as they will have to defend 25 seats. According to The Hill, these are the seven most vulnerable Senate seats. Sen. Dean Heller (R-Nev.): Heller is the only Republican up for reelection in 2018 who represents a state that Hillary Clinton won last November. Heller has also had a difficult 2017. Sen. Claire McCaskill (D-Mo.): McCaskill is one of the few remaining statewide Democratic officeholders in Missouri, which Trump won by 19 points in November. Sen. Joe Donnelly (D-Ind.): Donnelly used a bipartisan approach to politics and his appeal to blue-collar voters to win a Senate seat in 2012, but he will face another difficult race to keep the seat in a state Trump won by 19 points. Sen. Jeff Flake (R-Ariz.): Flake would not rank this high in a typical election year, but it is also unusual for a Republican president to threaten to support a primary challenge to an incumbent GOP senator. Sen. Joe Manchin (D-W.Va.): In 2016, West Virginia voted for Trump by a larger margin than any other state, 42 points. Sen. Heidi Heitkamp (D-N.D.): Heitkamp also represents a strongly Republican state; North Dakota voted for Trump by about 36 points. Sen. Jon Tester (D-Mont.): Republicans have favorable prospects in Montana. Trump won the state by more than 20 points in November, and Republican Greg Gianforte recently won the state’s at-large congressional seat in a special election even after he assaulted a reporter.
